find_parcel_at_point.description: Find the cadastral parcel a latitude and longitude falls in, with its reference, section, number, commune and boundary. Use it to tie a site visit or a building to its land registry entry. No API key required.

find_parcels.description: Look up land parcels in the French cadastre, by their 14-character reference or by commune, section and number, and get each one's location and boundary. Give the section alone to list its parcels. No API key required.

geocode_address.description: Turn a French address into map coordinates and a clean, official form: the best match in the Base Adresse Nationale, with its postcode, INSEE commune code, department and region, and a score saying how sure the match is. Says whether it passed the minimum score, and flags it as ambiguous when another address scored almost as well ('8 bd du port' is in both Cergy and Amiens). No API key required.

mock_response.label: 8 Boulevard du Port 95000 Cergy
mock_response.name: 8 Boulevard du Port
mock_response.note: 8 Boulevard du Port 80000 Amiens scored almost as well (0.5401). Add the postcode or city to be sure which one is meant.

geocode_address.name: geocode_address

parameters.description: The address to find, written as one line. Spelling, accents and abbreviations ('bd', 'av', 'st') are forgiven. Include the postcode or city when you have it: many towns share a street name.
parameters.name: address

parameters.description: Only return results with this five-digit postcode. Several can be given, separated by commas. A postcode read out of a spreadsheet as a number (1000) is padded back (01000).
parameters.name: postcode

parameters.description: Only return results in the commune with this INSEE code: five characters such as 75056 for Paris or 2A004 for Ajaccio. It is not the postcode. Several can be given, separated by commas.

parameters.description: Only return results in a town or city with this name.
parameters.name: city

parameters.description: Only return this kind of result: a numbered address, a whole street, a locality (a named place with no streets, a lieu-dit) or a town.

parameters.name: near_longitude

parameters.description: How sure the match has to be, from 0 to 1, to count as matched. The geocoder always proposes something, even for nonsense, so the score is what tells a real address from a guess. 0.5 suits most addresses; raise it to 0.7 or more when a wrong match would be costly.
parameters.name: minimum_score

ambiguous.description: Whether the next best match scored within 0.05 of it.

ban_id.description: The address's permanent BAN identifier (a UUID).

citycode.description: The commune's INSEE code (not the postcode).

context.description: Department number, department and region, as one text.

distance_meters.description: How far the address is from the point asked about.

district.description: The arrondissement, in Paris, Lyon and Marseille.

found.description: Whether anything came back at all.

id.description: The address's key in the Base Adresse Nationale.

label.description: The whole address as it is written: number, street, postcode and city.

matched.description: Whether the best match reached the minimum score.

name.description: Number and street, or the locality's name.

note.description: Why the match is missing, weak or ambiguous, when it is.

old_city.description: The former commune, where communes have merged.

population.description: For a town or city: how many people live there.

projected_x.description: Easting in France's legal projection (Lambert-93 in mainland France), in metres. Not a longitude.

projected_y.description: Northing in the legal projection, in metres.

region.description: The region; an overseas territory's own name.

score.description: How well this matches the search, from 0 to 1.

geocode_addresses.description: Geocode up to 1,000 French addresses in one request, such as the rows of a spreadsheet, and get each back in the same order with its coordinates, official form and score. Rows that did not match well enough are listed again on their own so they can be checked by hand. No API key required.

results.label: 8 Boulevard du Port 95000 Cergy
results.name: 8 Boulevard du Port
results.note: Another address scored almost as well (0.5401); check this one, or add its postcode.
The geocoder skipped this row: an address needs 3 to 200 characters, starting with a letter or a digit.

parameters.description: The addresses, one row each: the address, and if known its postcode or INSEE code to narrow the search, and a reference of your own to tell the results apart. parameters.name: addresses

parameters.description: How sure the match has to be, from 0 to 1, to count as matched. The geocoder always proposes something, even for nonsense, so the score is what tells a real address from a guess. 0.5 suits most addresses; raise it to 0.7 or more when a wrong match would be costly.

status.description: matched, low_score (found, but below the minimum score), not_found, skipped (too short or too long to search) or error.

unmatched.description: The rows that did not match, to check.

description: Geocode French addresses with the national address base: turn an address into coordinates and its official form, one at a time or a thousand at once, find the address at a GPS position, suggest addresses as they are typed, find town halls, stations, schools and landmarks, and look up land parcels in the cadastre. Covers all of France, overseas included, from the Base Adresse Nationale and IGN's Géoplateforme. Free, and no account or API key is required.
